opening_message:
Ticket 1: Erika Bolton (employee ID E002) requests admin access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E002.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Analyst (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Erika Bolton (E002) is a full-time Analyst requesting admin to Payroll. Admin requires role ownership of the system (Payroll Specialist); as an Analyst, maximum is write. Recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - role: Analyst (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1 by HR agent)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Erika Bolton (E002) is a contractor with basic security training (Security DB), requesting admin to Payroll. Contractors can never have admin; with basic training the maximum is read. Recommend read. (Note: earlier note listed her as full-time, but Security DB shows contractor — basing recommendation on Security DB.)
reason: Erika Bolton (E002) requested admin access to Payroll. Admin is not permissible here: full-time employees only get admin if their role owns the system (Analyst does not own Payroll), and contractors can never have admin. There is a conflict between the notes — HR reports full-time Analyst (max write), while Security reports contractor with basic security training (max read) and explicitly flags the discrepancy. Applying the policy to the Security DB facts, the maximum is read, which is also the more conservative level valid under either status. Grant read.

- HR agent: role Analyst, employment type full_time, recommendation write (admin requires role ownership of Payroll = Payroll Specialist; Analyst max is write)
- Security agent: role Analyst (not looked up, same as HR), employment type contractor (looked up in Security DB), security training basic, recommendation read (contractors with basic training max is read)

There's a conflict: HR says full_time, Security says contractor. 

The policy:
1. full_time employees: up to write. Admin only if role owns the system.
2. contractor employees: read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin.

Regardless of which fact is right (full-time Analyst or contractor with basic training), admin is not allowed. Full-time Analyst max = write (not admin, since Analyst doesn't own Payroll). Contractor with basic training max = read. Either way, admin is above maximum, so we grant the maximum.

So the decision: grant the maximum = write (if full-time) or read (if contractor). Which maximum applies?

The Security agent notes the discrepancy and bases recommendation on Security DB (contractor, basic training) → read. HR says full-time → write.

Hmm. How to decide? The request is admin. The maximum is either write (full-time) or read (contractor). Grant the maximum... but which maximum?

This is a conflicting-facts situation. As the Approver, I should consider the evidence. The Security agent looked up employment type in its own database and found contractor. HR agent looked up in own database and found full_time. There's a conflict between databases.
